title: Quiz Game

content.title: Your Mission
content.body:
You're about to build a quiz of anything you love — Pokémon, your family, soccer trivia, dinosaurs, world capitals, you pick. Let's go!

Your game should:
• Ask the player at least 3 questions using input()
• Check if each answer is correct using if/else
• Add 1 to the score for each correct answer
• Print the final score at the end

content.title: Quiz Ideas
content.body:
• A quiz about your favorite animal, movie, or sport
• A math challenge ("What is 7 × 8?")
• A geography quiz ("What's the largest ocean?")
• A Minecraft or Pokémon trivia quiz

Pick a topic you love!

content.title: Quick trick: .lower()
content.body: Quick trick: writing `answer.lower()` turns the player's text all lowercase. That way 'Blue', 'BLUE', and 'blue' all count as right — players don't get punished for capital letters.

content.title: Useful Patterns
content.body:
score = 0

answer = input("What color is the sky? ")
if answer.lower() == "blue":
    print("Correct! +1")
    score = score + 1
else:
    print("Not quite. The answer is blue.")

print("Your score:", score)

starterCode:

    print("Correct! +1")

    print("Correct! +1")

print("\nGame over! Your score:", score, "out of 2")
progressiveHints: Start with a score variable set to 0. Add 1 each time the player gets a question right.
Use input() to ask a question and store the answer in a variable.
Use if answer == "correct answer" to check if they got it right.
Use answer.lower() so the player can type 'Blue' or 'BLUE' and still get credit.
Copy your question pattern to add more questions — just change the question and the correct answer.

Full walkthrough — a complete tiny quiz you can copy and remix:

score = 0
q1 = input("What is 2 + 2? ")
if q1 == "4":
    print("Correct!")
    score = score + 1
q2 = input("What color is grass? ")
if q2.lower() == "green":
    print("Correct!")
    score = score + 1
print("Final score:", score)

milestones.label: Uses input() to ask a question

remixIdeas: Add a 4th and 5th question on your favorite topic.
Use a loop to repeat questions until the player gets them right.
Add difficulty levels — easy questions worth 1 point, hard ones worth 3.
Print a different message depending on the final score ("Amazing!", "Not bad!", "Try again!").
Turn it into a 2-player game — ask Player 1 then Player 2 and compare scores.
